notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: the Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. This is an EVENT draft: it is shorter than the prophet drafts, stays inside the event's own inventory refs and states only what those ayat state; the prophet stories (content/stories) are not repeated here. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

chapters.title_en: The pledge and the near victory

claims.statement_en: God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to the one addressed under the tree; He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquillity on them, rewarded them with a near victory and with abundant gains that they would take; God is Mighty, Wise.

God had promised them abundant gains that they would take; He hastened this one for them and held back the hands of people from them, so that it would be a sign for the believers and guide them to a straight path; and there was another gain that they were not able to take, which God had encompassed; God has power over all things.
Had those who disbelieved fought them, they would have turned their backs and then found no ally or helper; this is God's way that passed before, and no change will be found in God's way.

chapters.summary_md: God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance under the tree, and He sent down tranquillity on them and rewarded them with a near victory [c1]. He held back the hands of people from them, and said that no change will be found in His way [c2][c3].
chapters.body_md:
God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to the one addressed under the tree [c1]. He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquillity on them, rewarded them with a near victory and with abundant gains that they would take [c1].

God had promised them abundant gains that they would take; He hastened this one for them and held back the hands of people from them [c2]. This was so that it would be a sign for the believers and guide them to a straight path; and there was another gain that they were not able to take, which God had encompassed [c2].

Had those who disbelieved fought them, they would have turned their backs and then found no ally or helper [c3]. This is God's way that passed before, and no change will be found in God's way [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat link the pledge, God's knowledge of what was in the hearts, the tranquillity and the near victory in one sentence [c1]. They speak of gains in more than one way: gains that are taken now, and another gain they were not able to take, which God had encompassed [c2]. The statement about God's way is given as something that passed before and does not change [c3].
chapters.kids_md: The believers pledged allegiance under a tree, and God was pleased with them [c1]. God sent calm into their hearts and gave them a victory that was near [c1].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat tie God's pleasure to what He knew in their hearts [c1]. Another is that the ayat speak of God's way as one that does not change [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: where the tree was, when the pledge was given, or how many pledged; the ayat name neither the place nor the number.
- Not established: what the near victory was, or what the gains were; the ayat say only that they were near and abundant.
- Not established: who the people were whose hands were held back, or whether fighting had begun.
- Not established: whether these ayat describe a treaty; no treaty or its terms are mentioned in the verses cited.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name Hudaybiyyah for the place, the treaty and its terms, and the number of those who pledged. The detailed accounts rest on biographical and historical sources (sira) and on later reports that the repository does not yet hold.

claims.statement_en: They are those who disbelieved and barred the believers from the inviolable mosque and kept the offering from reaching its place; and had it not been for believing men and believing women whom the believers did not know, whom they might have trampled so that harm would have befallen them without knowing, God would have acted differently; this was so that God would admit into His mercy whom He wills; had they been distinct, God would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment.

When those who disbelieved set zeal in their hearts, the zeal of ignorance, God sent down His tranquillity on His Messenger and on the believers and made them keep to the word of piety, of which they were more worthy and more deserving.

God made true the vision of His Messenger: you will enter the inviolable mosque, if God wills, in safety, with your heads shaved or cut short, not fearing; He knew what they did not know, and made, besides that, a near victory.

chapters.summary_md: The ayat say that those who disbelieved barred the believers from the inviolable mosque, and that God sent down His tranquillity on His Messenger and on the believers [c1][c2]. They say that God made true the vision of His Messenger and made, besides that, a near victory [c3].
chapters.body_md:
They are those who disbelieved and barred the believers from the inviolable mosque and kept the offering from reaching its place [c1]. Had it not been for believing men and believing women whom the believers did not know, whom they might have trampled so that harm would have befallen them without knowing, God would have acted differently [c1]. This was so that God would admit into His mercy whom He wills [c1].

When those who disbelieved set zeal in their hearts, the zeal of ignorance, God sent down His tranquillity on His Messenger and on the believers [c2]. He made them keep to the word of piety, of which they were more worthy and more deserving [c2].

God made true the vision of His Messenger: you will enter the inviolable mosque, if God wills, in safety, with your heads shaved or cut short, not fearing [c3]. He knew what they did not know, and made, besides that, a near victory [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat place a barrier and a reason for restraint side by side: those who barred the believers, and believers among them whom the believers did not know [c1]. The tranquillity is named for the Messenger and the believers together [c2]. The last ayah gives a vision made true, a promise of entering in safety, and a near victory made besides [c3].
chapters.kids_md: Some people kept the believers away from the mosque [c1]. God sent calm to His Messenger and the believers, and said that He made true the vision of His Messenger [c2][c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat set the zeal of ignorance beside the tranquillity God sent down [c2]. Another is that the vision is joined to the words if God wills [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who barred them, where, when, or for how long; the ayat describe the barring and do not name the people or the place.
- Not established: what the offering was or how many were with it, or who the believing men and women they did not know were.
- Not established: when the vision was seen or what it showed beyond the entering and the shaved or shortened heads.
- Not established: whether the entering mentioned in the vision happened in the same year; the ayah says that God made, besides that, a near victory.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name of the place, the date and the sequence of events that these ayat are linked with.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the pledge, the barring and what followed. None is used in this draft.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Hudaybiyyah, the treaty, and the names of those involved.

48:24 is not drafted because it names a town, and the town's name is listed as a name from later tradition in the shared fixtures of this repository; a scholar should decide whether the draft may name it.
The Arabic word translated inviolable (a descriptive epithet of the mosque) is often rendered 'sacred'; a scholar should decide. The word translated 'vision' (ru'ya) can also be rendered 'dream'.
The phrase translated 'the word of piety' (kalimat al-taqwa) is rendered closely; its meaning is left to commentary.
